Page 2 worksheet: line 1 taxable income 34,250.00; no net long-term capital gain, so lines 2-10 are skipped and line 11 is 0.00; line 12 ordinary income tax from the PDF p18 rate table: 5.9% x 34,250.00 = 2,020.75, less 253 = 1,767.75; line 13 = 1,767.75, carried to page 1 line 8. Bracket schedule as numbers (the expected figure): 4.7% x 21,100.00 = 991.70; 5.9% x (34,250.00 - 21,100.00 = 13,150.00) = 775.85; bracket tax 1,767.55. The form gives 1,767.75; expected keeps the projection's 1,767.55, a difference of 0.20 from the table's whole-dollar constant (253 against 253.20). No Montana earned income: line 13 is the lesser of 50% x 50,000.00 = 25,000.00 and 0.00, so 0.00, and the booklet and the projection tax the whole pension.
accepted_approximations: The tables print a whole-dollar constant with the 5.9% rate (253, 506, 380) where the bracket arithmetic gives 253.20, 506.40, 380.40.
